title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a step in a coordinate-free, characteristic ≠ 2 rewrite of the classical Weierstrass theory, in preparation for describing level-2 moduli.

(52)-(54): The Weierstrass function is viewed as a degree-2 morphism ℘ : E → P^1_k. It identifies the quotient E/{±id_E} with a projective line (a k-form of P^1, here actually P^1_k). It is normalised by ℘(0_E) = ∞.

(55): The quotient map E → E/{±1} is canonical. The only freedom is the choice of coordinate on P^1 with ∞ fixed. So ℘ is determined up to affine changes ℘ ↦ a℘ + b, with a ∈ k^*, b ∈ k.

(56)-(57): The fixed points of −1 are the 2-torsion points. The three nonzero ones (ε_i)_{i∈I}, |I| = 3, are assumed k-rational, i.e. full level-2 structure. They go to three finite points ξ_i = ℘(ε_i) ∈ k. Together with ∞ these are the four branch points of the double cover, as Riemann-Hurwitz requires.

(58): The 'Weierstrass normalisation' Σξ_i = 0 kills the translation b. This needs 3 invertible (b = −Σξ_i/3). It leaves only the scaling ℘ ↦ a℘.

(59): In general one sets a_1 = −Σξ_i, a_2 = Σ_{i<j} ξ_iξ_j, a_3 = −Πξ_i. The next page completes this: z^3 + a_1z^2 + a_2z + a_3 = Π(z − ξ_i). With a tangent vector δ ∈ t_E linked to ℘ (℘ ~ δ^{⊗2}) and ℘' = θ_δ℘, one gets ℘'^2 = ℘^3 + a_1℘^2 + a_2℘ + a_3. This is consistent with the addition formula z_0 = λ^2 − a_1 − x_0 − y_0 on the previous page.

The NB in the margin seems to note the converse: from a projective line with distinct points (∞, ξ_i) one recovers an elliptic curve E_℘(ξ). This is the standard dictionary 'elliptic curve with level-2 structure ↔ P^1 with 4 marked distinct points', i.e. the λ-line.

The next page computes the involutions of P^1 induced by translation by ε_i. Overall purpose: an explicit description of the moduli of elliptic curves with level-2 structure (char ≠ 2) and of the action on it.
errors: No mathematical errors. Two things are left implicit: the ξ_i lie in k only because the 2-torsion is assumed k-rational (ε_i ∈ ₂E(k)); and the ξ_i must be distinct, which is equivalent to smoothness.
The a_i here are the elementary symmetric coefficients of the monic cubic y^2 = x^3 + a_1x^2 + a_2x + a_3. They are not Tate's a_1,…,a_6, a potential source of confusion.
The equation label (57) is missing in the manuscript for the ξ_i line.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but entirely classical setup of the Weierstrass/Legendre form with full level-2 structure. Nothing new beyond Grothendieck's intrinsic bookkeeping (℘ tied to a tangent vector).
transcription_corrections: Missing equation number (57) before 'ξ_i = ℘(ε_i) ∈ P^1_k(k) ∖ {∞} = k'.

The margin note is very hard to read; it is plausibly 'NB On obtient ainsi des E_℘(ξ), ξ ... quel que soit ... projectif ... distincts', i.e. a remark on the converse construction from distinct points on a projective line. The machine reading is unreliable.
